newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT to cut international call rates.
newsitem.headline: PLDT to cut international call rates.

text.p: The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) is seeking a cut in international toll rates due to stiffer competition and pressure from inter-connecting foreign telephone companies, officials said on Tuesday.
Rate increases for basic phone charges and call metering have also been sought to compensate for the international toll reduction, PLDT senior vice president Antonio Samson told reporters.
Until now, PLDT has subsidised local calls through its international services.
Subscribers were charged a fixed monthly subscription under which they were entitled to an unlimited numer of local calls as the exchanges did not have a metering system.
Stiff competition from new local telephone firms had prompted PLDT to readjust its rates, Samson said.
Telephone companies in the Philippines have to seek the approval of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to change tariffs.
Samson said the PLDT had applied to the NTC for a rate increase of between 31 and 45 percent on basic monthly charges as well as a restructuring of national long distance call rates.
It had also sought to lower call rates to the United States to 121.50 pesos from the present 152.55 pesos for the first three minutes, he said.
Charges to other countries such as Hong Kong, Japan and Saudi Arabia, where many Filipinos work, would also be cut, Samson said.
U.S. telephone companies have been pressing for a steep cut in international tariffs in a bid to generate more calls.
At present, the rate between the U.S. and the Philippines is $1 per minute and U.S. firms have sought to cut it to 38 cents per minute.
Calls to the U.S. comprise the bulk of PLDT's international call revenues.
Samson declined to say how the rate adjustments would affect PLDT's profits saying the NTC was yet to fix the new tariffs.
